proposal.look: THE STACK. The rock is dead hardware piled up: every face reads as thin courses of slab -- boards, drives, casings -- laid one on another, every other one a shade darker, a joint here and there; one course a block carries a strip of tarnished gold: an edge connector. A ridge's top is the top board, seamed once a block. Light: dull sage and solder-mask green; the floor is ash-brown grit with a chip of board lying in it (ROUTE 3 is ASHFALL); the bright floor patches become pale drifts.
proposal.split: SPLIT UMBRAL ASCENT (palette split now: a cold violet dusk, the same courses; its own tiles in batch G). THE WRONG WAY and the tunnel can keep the stack.

places: TAPPOINT (Diglett) 'sits under the route everything takes and reads what goes past' -- a wiretap's burrow
proposal.look: THE LINE. A long burrow of warm packed earth under the routes, and along the top of every cut runs the buried cable it was dug to reach: a red sheath over a dark core, two pixels deep, following the cut wherever it turns. The faces are packed clods; the ground above is calm earth with soft rises; TAPPOINT's holes are kept. Light: umber and ochre; the cable is the one colour that is not earth.
proposal.split: No split: TANOBY KEY is one room and an earth room suits it.

proposal.look: THE OUTAGE. Basalt that grew in the dark: the walls are tall columns, cut vertically (the stack runs across; this runs down), each column a lit left edge and a dark right one. Light: night indigo and blue-black, deep but never grey -- HALFTONE and the unread DOLDRUM own grey. VERBOSE (FLASH) shows it; unlit it is a 24-pixel circle in black.
proposal.split: SPLIT OTHER CAVE (palette split): the same columns in a palette that is not THE BLACKOUT's -- a pale mineral teal. A per-entry palette swap would make it never the same twice: described (how, cost, risks) in --draft's groups.json, not built; that is the user's question.

other_cave_per_entry: HOW: OTHER CAVE gets its own Tileset header (the palette split above) whose palettes are a table of N lights instead of one -- the mineral teal and, say, three more (amber, rose quartz, lichen). LoadTilesetPalette() in src/fieldmap.c already special-cases gTileset_General; one more case, `if (tileset == &gTileset_OtherCave)`, loads rows 7..12 from light number VAR_OTHER_CAVE_LIGHT instead of the header's own.

WHEN IT CHANGES: on ENTRY, never on a reload. LoadSecondaryTilesetPalette() also runs after a battle, after the bag or the menu closes, on a load from the save and on the DEBUG menu's return -- a light picked there would flicker mid-visit. So the map's ON_TRANSITION script (which runs once per warp in) steps the var: `addvar VAR_OTHER_CAVE_LIGHT, 1` mod N, or a `random N`. Stepping in order makes it a cycle a player can learn; random makes it never knowable (and can repeat the last one unless re-rolled).

COST: N x 192 bytes of palettes (rows 7..12; 768 B for four) plus about 40 bytes of code and one var (a free VAR_ 0x40xx). No tile, no metatile, no map changes. The watch's dusk/night tint and DaemonsIsHalftone() work on the loaded rows, so they apply on top unchanged.

RISKS: the field-move banners and the VERBOSE/FLASH fade reload palettes from the header (T-442's lesson): each such reload must go through the same case, or the cave snaps back to light 0 mid-visit -- check every caller of LoadSecondaryTilesetPalette and of gMapHeader.mapLayout->secondaryTileset->palettes. The wild encounters could follow the light (a different table per light, which is what Altering Cave's name promised in vanilla); that is a design question, not a palette one.
